The season began on 23 August 2013 and ended on 6 April 2014.{{cite web |title=جدول الدوري |url=http://www.slstat.com/spl2013-2014ar/champtable.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160705005713/http://www.slstat.com/spl2013-2014ar/champtable.php |archive-date=5 July 2016 |url-status=dead}} [[Al Fateh SC|Al-Fateh]] were the [[2012–13 Saudi Professional League|defending champions]] having won their first title last season.{{cite web |title=الفتح يحقق لقب الدوري للمرة الأولى في تاريخه |url=https://www.alriyadh.com/826251}} The league was contested by the 12 teams from the [[2012–13 Saudi Pro League|2012–13 season]] as well as [[Al-Nahda Club (Saudi Arabia)|Al-Nahda]] and [[Al-Orobah FC|Al-Orobah]], who joined as the promoted clubs from the [[2012–13 Saudi First Division|2012–13 First Division]]. They replace [[Al Wehda FC|Al-Wehda]] and [[Hajer FC|Hajer]] who were relegated to the [[2013–14 Saudi First Division|2013–14 First Division]]. On 28 March, [[Al-Nassr FC|Al-Nassr]] secured their seventh league title with one game to spare after a 1–1 draw away to [[Al Shabab FC (Riyadh)|Al-Shabab]].{{cite web |title=النصر بطلاً لدوري جميل 2014 |url=https://www.alriyadh.com/922240}} This was Al-Nassr's first league title since the [[1994–95 Saudi Premier League|1994–95 season]]. [[Al-Nahda Club (Saudi Arabia)|Al-Nahda]] were the first team to be relegated following a 2–2 home draw with [[Al-Orobah FC|Al-Orobah]] on 22 March.{{cite web |title="ديربي بريدة" سلبي.. ورسمياً النهضة يهبط لدوري "ركاء" |url=https://sabq.org/EQUfde?w=c}} [[Al-Ettifaq FC|Al-Ettifaq]] became the second and final team to be relegated following a 2–1 defeat away to [[Al-Ahli Saudi FC|Al-Ahli]] on the final matchday.{{cite web |title=الراشد يحرز هدف في مرمى فريقه ويهبط به إلى "ركاء" |url=https://www.alriyadh.com/924732}} Al-Ettifaq were relegated for the first time in history after 37 consecutive seasons in the top flight. ==Name sponsorship== On 14 April 2013, it was that the [[Abdul Latif Jameel]] group had signed a six-year sponsorship contract with the SAFF.{{cite web |title=رسمياً.. إطلاق اسم "دوري عبداللطيف جميل" على الدوري السعودي الممتاز |url=https://www.sadacom.news/news/s/13093}} Starting from the 2013–14 season, the league would be known as the '''Abdul Latif Jameel Professional League'''. It was later announced that the sponsorship deal cost [[Saudi riyal|SAR]]720 million in total, [[Saudi riyal|SAR]]120 million a year. The previous sponsor, [[Zain Saudi Arabia|Zain]], opted not to renew their contract following its expiration. ==Teams== Fourteen teams competed in the league – the twelve teams from the previous season and the two teams promoted from the [[2012–13 Saudi First Division|First Division]]. The promoted teams were [[Al-Orobah FC|Al-Orobah]] (playing in the top flight for the first time ever) and [[Al-Nahda Club (Saudi Arabia)|Al-Nahda]] (returning to the top flight after nineteen years).
